newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end up on local buying of blue chip.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end up on local buying of blue chip.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up on Tuesday as local institutions, who have been on the sidelines, entered the market in a big way, brokers said.
The all share closed 4.7 points higher at 634.46 on a turnover of 104.4 million rupees. The last time the turnover topped the 100 million rupee mark was on January 16.
Making up the turnover were local buying of 500,700 shares of Commercial Bank at 156 and 163 rupees per share and 48,000 Hayleys at 210 rupees per share, brokers said.
"Local buyers are realising they have to come in and match sellers at these levels," said Thikshan Arulampalam of brokerage Lanka Securities.
"We might see more transactions from local institutions in the days to come," he said.
Other brokers said local investors may still continue to be selective ahead of next week's local elections.
"It is possible that Commercial was a one-off case. It could be that a particular party outwatching a large quantity found it," said Ajit Dias Wanigasekera of Ceylinco Stock Brokers.

On Tuesday, gains outnumbered losses 32 to 10. Hayleys gained nine rupees. National Development Bank was up two rupees to 203 rupees. Foreign buying outstripped selling 4.5 million rupees to 2.2 million.
